clips.text_zh: Tesla又跌11%，冇fucking reason。成間公司根本係meme。你睇吓delivery、earnings同Musk個網號，仲有邊個正常人企穩。
clips.text_en_b1: Tesla crashed 11% for no fucking reason. The entire company is a meme. Delivery numbers, earnings, and Musk’s online posts were probably part of the story, but the OP gives no proper reason for the crash. Anonymous traders are left guessing what happened next.
clips.text_en_b2: Tesla crashed by 11% for absolutely no fucking reason, because the entire company increasingly looks like a meme rather than a serious business. Delivery figures, earnings, and Musk’s online posts were probably connected to the sell-off, although the original poster offered no solid explanation. As anonymous traders scramble to work out what happened and what may come next, confidence in the company appears to be draining away fast.
clips.text_en_c1: Tesla crashed 11% for no fucking reason, which is precisely what makes the episode so absurd. The entire company increasingly feels like a meme rather than a functioning business. Delivery figures, earnings, and Musk’s online posts were probably part of the story, but the OP offers no proper explanation for the collapse. If no coherent catalyst exists, anonymous traders are left speculating about what happened, what might happen next, and whether the stock can possibly recover any credibility.
clips.text_en_c2: Tesla has slumped another 11%, ostensibly without the faintest fucking reason. The company, increasingly, resembles a speculative meme rather than a functioning automotive enterprise, with delivery figures, earnings and Musk’s erratic online commentary apparently woven into the explanation. Yet the original poster offers no coherent account of what triggered the sell-off. Anonymous traders are therefore left to reconstruct the narrative from fragments, trading rumours and whatever interpretation happens to suit their positions. Nobody appears confident, although collective uncertainty has proved exceptionally effective at driving the share price lower.
clips.source_hint: A /biz/ post complaining that Tesla fell 11% without a clear reason.

clips.text_zh: The Cybertruck is dead. Musk’s terrible, awful, no-good week continues. Tesla delivery同earnings一齊畀人串，連Cybertruck都頂唔順，個股就繼續寄。
clips.text_en_b1: The Cybertruck is dead. Musk’s terrible, awful, no-good week continues. The post links Tesla’s falling fortunes to the Cybertruck and Musk’s bad week, while anonymous traders argue about what the vehicle’s problems mean for the company.
clips.text_en_b2: The Cybertruck is dead, and Musk’s terrible, awful, no-good week is dragging the company down with it. Tesla’s falling fortunes were linked to both disappointing delivery numbers and weak earnings, while the Cybertruck struggled to cope with the bad publicity. As anonymous traders argue over whether these problems are temporary or evidence of something much deeper, the stock continued its relentless descent.
clips.text_en_c1: The Cybertruck is dead, and Musk’s terrible, awful, no-good week continues apace. The post connects Tesla’s rapidly deteriorating fortunes with the Cybertruck, whose mounting problems have become impossible for investors to ignore. Tesla’s delivery numbers and earnings are being scrutinised at the same time, leaving the company with little room for further disappointment. As anonymous traders debate what the vehicle’s failures signal for Tesla’s broader strategy, the stock is forced to keep sending a very negative message.
clips.text_en_c2: The Cybertruck is dead, or at least financially indistinguishable from it. Musk’s wretched, no-good week, to put it mildly, has continued to unspool. The post attributes Tesla’s deteriorating fortunes to the Cybertruck, whose recurrent problems have become inseparable from the broader question of whether the company can manufacture anything other than controversy at scale. Earnings and delivery data have also come under fire, compounding the reputational damage and leaving the stock to sink further. Anonymous traders argue over whether the vehicle’s failures signal a deeper crisis at Tesla or merely reflect the usual turbulence surrounding Musk and his pronouncements.
clips.source_hint: A /biz/ post declaring the Cybertruck dead during Musk’s bad week.

clips.text_zh: 靠AI續命啦。Claude Fable 5.2由一個空folder開始，coordinate超過1,000個subagents，連續八日寫code、測試同review。最後真係boot到個operating system出嚟。
clips.text_en_b1: Claude Fable 5.2 builds an operating system from scratch. One Anthropic engineer gave the model a prototype operating system to design. Starting from an empty folder, it coordinated over 1,000 subagents for eight days, writing, testing, and reviewing code. It produced a working OS that boots on a laptop.
clips.text_en_b2: Claude Fable 5.2 has built an operating system from scratch, which sounds like the setup for an AI disaster movie but apparently became reality. One Anthropic engineer gave the model a prototype operating system to design. Starting with an empty folder, it coordinated more than 1,000 subagents for eight straight days, writing, testing, and reviewing code. In the end, it produced a working OS capable of booting on a laptop.
clips.text_en_c1: Claude Fable 5.2 has built an operating system from scratch, suggesting that AI might already be capable of sustaining a project of considerable complexity. One Anthropic engineer gave the model a prototype operating system to design. Beginning with an empty folder, it coordinated more than 1,000 subagents for eight consecutive days, writing, testing, and reviewing code throughout. In the end, it produced a functioning OS that successfully boots on a laptop, turning an initially vague concept into usable software.
clips.text_en_c2: Claude Fable 5.2 has apparently kept itself alive by building an operating system from nothing. An Anthropic engineer supplied the model with a prototype OS and a blank folder, after which it orchestrated more than 1,000 subagents for eight consecutive days. Those agents wrote code, ran tests, reviewed one another’s work and iterated through whatever errors emerged, turning an initially empty directory into a functioning system. The decisive achievement is not abstract fluency in programming, but sustained coordination across an enormous workforce without the operation collapsing into chaos. The final operating system reportedly boots successfully on a laptop, an engineering feat that blurs the line between an AI coding tool and an autonomous development team.
clips.source_hint: A /g/ post claiming Claude Fable 5.2 coordinated 1,000 subagents to build a working operating system.

clips.text_zh: 點解咁多男人fucking depressed？就算睇porn、埋堆女人都未必 cheer up 到。單身、30歲、返工再考牌，loneliness 真係可以當個glitch，唔係人生設定。
clips.text_en_b1: Why are so many men fucking depressed now? Even porn and women aren’t cheering them up. The thread asks whether casual sex, relationships, and familiar entertainment can really fix loneliness, or whether depression needs a more serious answer.
clips.text_en_b2: Why are so many men fucking depressed these days? Even porn, casual sex, relationships, and familiar entertainment may fail to cheer them up. The thread questions whether these superficial distractions can genuinely deal with loneliness, or whether men need a more serious and honest conversation about their mental health. Being single, turning thirty, working constantly, and studying for another qualification can make life feel increasingly hollow, even when nobody can identify one obvious cause.
clips.text_en_c1: Why are so many men fucking depressed now? Even porn, casual sex, and spending time with women do not necessarily make them feel any better. The thread asks whether relationships, sex, and familiar entertainment can genuinely relieve loneliness, or whether depression requires a far more serious response. It also reflects the pressures men face while being single, turning thirty, working, and studying for another qualification. Loneliness can behave like a system glitch, but it is certainly not a sensible default setting for life.
clips.text_en_c2: Why are so many men fucking depressed nowadays? Even pornography and women do not reliably raise their spirits, which suggests that casual sex, relationships and familiar entertainment may offer fleeting distraction rather than genuine relief. The thread asks a difficult question: can loneliness truly be cured through conventional remedies, or does depression demand a more serious reckoning? Its examples are unmistakably recognisable—being thirty, working, studying for another qualification, and remaining single despite doing everything society suggests should make happiness attainable. Loneliness, in this sense, feels less like a personal failing and more like a glitch in the default settings of adult life, for which the prescribed solutions are conspicuously inadequate.
clips.source_hint: A /pol/ thread asking why so many men are depressed despite porn and women.

clips.text_zh: 三個月gym都唔大件，我真係廢。日常三組10至12下：Monday chest同triceps，Tuesday back同biceps。變化好淺，係咪programme根本唔work？
clips.text_en_b1: Why am I not growing? I’ve been hitting the gym for three months and noticed only faint changes. I feel like my chest and triceps are the only muscles growing. I do three sets of 10–12 reps, starting with five-minute treadmill cardio, bench press, incline dumbbell press, dips, cable fly, and triceps pushdown on Monday.
clips.text_en_b2: Why am I not growing after three months of training? I have noticed only faint changes and feel as though my chest and triceps are the only muscles that are responding. I do three sets of 10–12 repetitions, beginning with five minutes of treadmill cardio, then bench press, incline dumbbell press, dips, cable fly, and triceps pushdown on Monday. Although my programme seems solid, the disappointing progress makes me wonder whether it is actually working.
clips.text_en_c1: Why am I not growing after three months at the gym? The changes I notice are painfully faint, and I feel as though only my chest and triceps are developing. I perform three sets of 10–12 repetitions, beginning each session with five minutes of treadmill cardio. On Monday, my routine includes bench presses, incline dumbbell presses, dips, cable flyes, and triceps pushdowns. Since the progress is so limited, I am beginning to wonder whether my programme is fundamentally flawed rather than simply too short.
clips.text_en_c2: Why am I not growing? After three months of regular training, the changes are faint enough to make me wonder whether the programme is working at all. My chest and triceps appear to be developing, but the gains elsewhere remain elusive. The routine begins with five minutes on the treadmill before three sets of 10–12 repetitions, with Monday devoted to chest and triceps and Tuesday to back and biceps. The exercises include the bench press, incline dumbbell press, dips, cable fly and triceps pushdown. Three months, however, is a very short window, and the absence of visible transformation does not necessarily indicate that the programme is fundamentally flawed.
clips.source_hint: A /fit/ post asking why three months of training has produced little visible muscle growth.

clips.text_zh: 今日最離譜題目：將動畫或漫畫premise改写成The Twilight Zone。例子係Ataru Moroboshi，自以為係世界最強lothario，但其他人只覺得佢係煩人病秧，成個世界已經變成異空間。
clips.text_en_b1: ITT: Rewrite the premise of an anime or manga as a Twilight Zone episode. This young man is Ataru Moroboshi. In his own mind, he is the world’s greatest lothario. To his family, associates, and disputed friends, he is only a perfunctory and pestiferous presence. This came up on /a/ tonight.
clips.text_en_b2: Today’s most absurd prompt: rewrite the premise of an anime or manga as an episode of The Twilight Zone. One example is Ataru Moroboshi, who believes himself to be the world’s greatest lothario and expects every attractive woman to fall for him. In reality, however, his family, associates, and disputed friends regard him as a superficial, irritating, and sickly presence. The ordinary world around him has become a strange Twilight Zone in which nobody sees the hero he imagines.
clips.text_en_c1: Today’s most absurd prompt: rewrite the premise of an anime or manga as an episode of The Twilight Zone. The example is Ataru Moroboshi, a young man who believes himself to be the world’s greatest lothario. In his own mind, every encounter confirms his irresistible status; however, to his family, associates, and disputed friends, he is merely a perfunctory, pestiferous presence whose company makes ordinary life unbearable. The idea emerged on /a/ tonight, and it captures the series’ uncanny ability to make familiar relationships deeply strange.
clips.text_en_c2: Today’s most peculiar prompt is to recast the premise of an anime or manga as an episode of The Twilight Zone. The chosen example is Ataru Moroboshi, a young man who considers himself the world’s greatest lothario. In his own estimation, every encounter confirms his charm, sophistication and romantic supremacy. To his family, associates and—according to the disputed account—his friends, however, he is merely perfunctory, irritating and relentlessly pestiferous. The premise works because its central conflict lies not between competing heroes, but between Ataru’s self-delusion and everyone else’s bewildered recognition of the truth. It surfaced on /a/ tonight.
clips.source_hint: An /a/ thread rewriting anime premises as Twilight Zone episodes, using Ataru Moroboshi as the example.
